status_issues.source_status: The source credits Harborth (1974) with proving the triangular-lattice formula, and more generally f₂(m) = floor(3m − sqrt(12m − 3)) for m ≥ 2.
status_issues.evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1084 explicitly displays f₂(3n² + 3n + 1) = 9n² + 3n and immediately says: “Harborth [Ha74b] proved this, and more generally …”. The bibliography identifies [Ha74b] as Harborth, Lösung zu Problem 664A (1974). The n = 0 instance in Lean is the elementary identity f₂(1) = 0.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change this variant's category to research solved and cite Harborth [Ha74b]. The Lean equality itself need not change.

reformulations.difference: The universal dimension statement allows arbitrary Kakeya sets, rather than restricting to compact sets as in another common formulation mentioned in IsKakeya's documentation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Keleti–Máthé Theorem 1.1 supplies a compact Kakeya set of a minimum Hausdorff dimension d and proves that every arbitrary Kakeya set has dimension at least d. Thus, if all compact Kakeya sets have dimension n, then d = n and all arbitrary Kakeya sets also have dimension n. The converse follows by restriction to compact sets. This verifies the equivalence of the conjectures, not an equivalence of the compact and noncompact set predicates.

reformulations.difference: Besides equality of the extended-real suprema, Lean explicitly includes an equivalence of boundedness above for the two ranges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Equality of the extended-real suprema transfers every finite upper bound in either direction, so it already implies the boundedness equivalence. I proved the conjunction equivalent to the supremum equality in /workspace/review/sup_equivalence.lean; no differentiability assumption is needed for this redundancy.

review.notes: The reviewed module contains only the scoped notation ℝ^n := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). It agrees exactly with Mathlib and the standard real Euclidean coordinate space; no competing Mathlib notation with this spelling was found. Checked its interpretation in all 13 direct problem users, the graph-embedding wrapper, and that wrapper's Erdős 1007 consumer. No mismatch in the meaning of this notation was found. Successful Lean experiments in scratch.lean and use_sites.lean verify dimension n, the dot product and Pythagorean distance, norm (3,4) = 5, the usual coordinate topology and volume, the singleton R^0 with no unit directions, R^1 distance, and relevant zero-dimensional use-site boundaries. These files are under /workspace/review; the reviewed file still matches its committed blob. MathOverflow 235893 also contains a very recent, explicitly unverified counterexample claim requesting independent verification; I did not treat that claim as an established status change. This review's consumer checks concern the meaning of the Euclidean-space notation, not a full independent audit of every other definition in those problem files.
